messages:
maria: FYI I'm trying the "adapter-stitch" route for CustomerX LoRA v2 — want to validate compatibility before we bake it into the hosted model pool. can folks run compat checks and a quick eval pack?

ashish: on it. quick note: the adapter was trained against fp16 base but customer requested an 8-bit/4-bit quantized serving path, so merging might be noisy. will run compat-check script.

ashish: ran: `python tools/compat-check.py --base gpt-jax-20b-fp16 --adapter customerx-lora-v2`
```
Checking shapes... OK
Bias config mismatch: adapter has bias=true, base bias=false
Found kv-cache layout v1 vs v2 -> potential mismatch
Quantization safe-check: FAILED (per-layer scale mismatch on attn.q_proj)
```
ashish: TL;DR: merge possible but needs patching for bias flags and a small rebase to align kv layout.

leo: does eval-bot have the quick pack results for customer prompts? want to see instruction-following/regression after stitch.

eval-bot: quick-eval pack "customerx_smoke_v1" finished. metrics (post-merge simulated):
- instr-acc: 0.86 -> 0.78 (regression)
- rouge-l: 0.52 -> 0.50
- latency (p50) +3ms for fp16 baseline, +12ms for 4-bit path
- hallucination-rate (heuristic) went from 4% -> 9%

sara: that's bigger than I'd expect. Did you run eval on the runtime-apply (delta-only) mode vs static-merge?

eval-bot: ran both: static-merge shows the instr-acc drop. runtime-apply (adapter applied at inference time) keeps instr-acc at 0.85 but increases tail latency ~22ms.

leo: so two tradeoffs: static merge = lower tail latency but quality regressions unless we fix bias/kv; runtime-apply = better quality but higher latency. customer SLA?

customerx-pm: they'd accept +20ms if quality is better. they care more about answer correctness than tight latencies.

ashish: plan: 1) patch adapter bias flags + small rebase to base kv layout; 2) run targeted quantization-aware merge (there's a new option in stitcher: `--quant-aware`), 3) run eval pack again (full customer prompts).

maria: sounds good. ashish, can you add a short reproducible script to the PR so SWE on the infra side can validate later? also include the eval pack commands.

ashish: will open PR with `tools/stitcher/merge_customerx.sh` that: downloads base fp16, applies adapter, runs `stitcher --quant-aware --bias-fix`, outputs merged.pt and an eval manifest.

ashish: sample output snippet from stitcher dry-run:
```
stitcher dry-run
base: gpt-jax-20b-fp16
adapter: customerx-lora-v2
quant-aware check: ok for attn proj after bias-fix
merged params estimate: +0.6GB
recommended serving mode: runtime-apply if 4-bit strict
```

leo: @maria can infra try a canary on dedicated GPU pool with runtime-apply first (since customer allows latency increase) while ashish works on a clean static merge? that gives customer a path quickly.

maria: yes let's canary runtime-apply. deploy-bot, can you schedule a canary slot tomorrow 09:00 UTC on dedicated-small?

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: 2026-06-01T09:00:00Z -> dedicated-small, 2 instances, route only for customerx traffic. :white_check_mark:

customerx-pm: appreciated. can you also share expected ETA for static merged validation?

ashish: target timeline: bias/kv patch + quant-aware merge + full eval run = 48h. will ping when PR is up.

maria: action items: (1) ashish PR + reproducible script, (2) infra canary runtime-apply tomorrow 09:00 UTC, (3) eval pack full run post-merge and compare metrics, (4) if static merge stable, promote to dedicated pool with fallback to runtime-apply. I'll coordinate release notes and rollback playbook.

leo: I'll add a quick grafana dashboard panel for the canary: instr-acc, hallucination-rate, latency p50/p95.

sara: also add a prompt subset with the critical billing/cc-handling examples — their worst-case failures are there.

maria: thanks all. ashish, ping the thread when PR is ready and include the eval artifacts link.

ashish: will do. thanks! :rocket:
